newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures closed lower but well off their lows as investors overcame some fears of a German interest rate increase.

Traders also cited firmness in the U.S. bond market and the strength of the dollar as supporting factors, lifting the notionnel from its low of 130.34 to close at 130.60, 18 points off the high of 130.74.
Dealers and analysts said that despite the Bundesbank's failure to set repo rates more than two weeks ahead, they did not believe in a German rate rise.
The Bundesbank's move was seen as a signal it was ready to raise rates if needed to defend the mark, they said.

"The fundamentals of the German economy do not justify a rate increase," said one dealer. "And monetary union is just too important," he added, referring to the feeling expressed by market analysts that a rate increase by the Bundesbank would be seen as anti single currency and could actually damage prospects for its success by slowing economic growth in Europe.

They said that the mark's weakness was really dollar and sterling strength, noting that the mark had barely moved against the franc in recent days. In late afternoon, the mark was trading at 3.3711 francs, virtually unmoved from its level early this morning, and the dollar was worth 1.8354 marks.
The market will look ahead to next week's U.S. figures of July consumer confidence, second quarter GDP and, most importantly, Friday's July payrolls report.
